bib.title: Pixel Recurrent Neural Networks
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 33rd International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), New York, NY, USA, 2016 (arXiv v3)

question: Can a deep autoregressive network over discrete raw pixel values give an expressive, tractable and scalable model of natural image distributions?
hypothesis: Larger receptive fields, deeper recurrent stacks with residual connections and a discrete softmax output improve image log-likelihood.
contributions: Row LSTM and Diagonal BiLSTM layers, plus the fully convolutional PixelCNN and a Multi-Scale PixelRNN
Discrete softmax over 256 pixel values and residual connections for LSTM layers up to 12 deep
Log-likelihood better than previous results on MNIST and CIFAR-10
First likelihood benchmarks on ImageNet at 32x32 and 64x64

method.summary: Images are factorised pixel by pixel in raster order and RGB channel by channel; each conditional is a 256-way softmax predicted by a stack of masked convolutions and 2D LSTM layers (Row LSTM, Diagonal BiLSTM) or a masked-convolution PixelCNN. Trained by maximum likelihood on MNIST, CIFAR-10 and downsampled ImageNet.

datasets.name: MNIST (binary version)
datasets.source: LeCun et al. 1998; binarised per Salakhutdinov & Murray 2008

datasets.name: CIFAR-10
datasets.split: validation set for ablations, test set for Table 5
datasets.preprocessing: scaling and centering only; no data augmentation

datasets.name: ImageNet (ILSVRC) downsampled to 32x32 and 64x64
datasets.source: Russakovsky et al. 2015; downsampled images released at image-net.org/small/download.php
datasets.preprocessing: scaling and centering only; no data augmentation

models.name: PixelRNN Row LSTM
models.architecture: 7x7 mask-A conv, residual Row LSTM layers (i-s 3x1 mask B, s-s 3x1 unmasked), two ReLU+1x1 mask-B conv layers, 256-way softmax per RGB colour
models.context: triangular receptive field above the pixel

other.top 1x1 conv layers: 1024 feature maps for CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, 32 for MNIST

models.name: PixelRNN Diagonal BiLSTM
models.architecture: as Row LSTM but i-s 1x1 mask B and s-s 2x1 unmasked kernels on skewed diagonals

models.name: PixelCNN
models.architecture: fully convolutional, 3x3 mask-B convs with residual blocks, no pooling

models.name: Multi-Scale PixelRNN
models.architecture: unconditional PixelRNN generates s x s subsampled image; conditional PixelRNN biased by deconvolution-upsampled map generates n x n image

training.objective: negative log-likelihood of discrete (multinomial/softmax) pixel distribution; sigmoid for binary MNIST
training.lr_schedule: set manually per dataset to the highest values that allowed fast convergence (values not given)
training.regularisation: small batch size of 16 'seems to regularize the models'; no augmentation
training.hardware: GPUs (type and count not given), Torch toolbox

other.preprocessing: scaling and centering of inputs only

inference.decoding: sequential ancestral sampling, pixel by pixel in raster order, RGB in order; each sampled pixel fed back into the network
inference.prompting: image completions by conditioning on the unoccluded pixels (Fig 1, Fig 9)

other.parallelism: training and test-set likelihood evaluation are parallel over positions; generation is sequential for both PixelRNN and PixelCNN

metrics.name: negative log-likelihood (bits/dim)
metrics.definition: total discrete log-likelihood normalised by image dimensionality (e.g. 32x32x3=3072 for CIFAR-10); comparable to continuous models via uniform dequantisation

baselines: DBM, DBN, NADE, EoNADE, DLGM, DARN, MADE, DRAW (MNIST)
Uniform, Multivariate Gaussian, NICE, Deep Diffusion, Deep GMMs, RIDE (CIFAR-10)
eval.protocol: single reported number per model; no seeds, error bars or significance tests; qualitative sample inspection

evidence.quote: For smaller datasets such as MNIST and CIFAR-10 we use smaller batch sizes of 16 images as this seems to regularize the models.

limits: No ImageNet baselines exist, so Table 6 is only a benchmark.
Learning rates, step counts, epochs, compute, parameter counts and seeds are not stated; single runs, no error bars.
RIDE result is by personal communication.
Authors say model size is constrained by computation time and GPU memory.
ImageNet 64x64 model differs from others (4 layers, no residual) so is not an ablation of scale.
Sample quality assessed qualitatively only; CIFAR-10 images likely resized differently from ImageNet ones, so cross-dataset NLL is not directly comparable.

terms.definition: Mask A, used only on the first conv layer, blocks a colour's connection to itself; mask B, used in later layers, also allows the connection from a colour to itself.

lineage.work: Generative image modeling using spatial LSTMs (Theis & Bethge)
lineage.note: 2D LSTM image model it advances to large scale; MCGSM ablation
lineage.quote: A two-dimensional RNN has produced very promising results in modeling grayscale images and textures (Theis & Bethge, 2015).
